rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, all design decisions are uncertain. The most informative first experiment is a minimal, well-understood baseline that establishes a performance floor for all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) uses the simplest profile setting and the most standard, interpretable RNA encoder (PCA), isolating the contribution of RNA data alone without confounding from image modality, learned encoders, or multi-profile aggregation. This baseline will let me quantify how much additional value each design axis (image modality, learned encoders, multiprofile aggregation, multimodal fusion) contributes in later experiments. Starting from the simplest configuration maximizes interpretability of every future delta and is the most efficient use of the first experiment under a limited budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality adds predictive signal at all — the core premise of multimodal cellular profiling. Config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is the cleanest controlled extension of the baseline: it keeps the RNA encoder and profile setting identical to config_001, so any accuracy difference is attributable to the addition of image features via a standard resnet50 encoder and simple concat fusion. This single experiment simultaneously tests (a) whether image modality carries complementary information, (b) whether concat fusion is a viable starting point, and (c) whether resnet50 is a reasonable image encoder. If config_016 substantially exceeds 48.5%, we exploit the multimodal direction in subsequent runs; if it is comparable or worse, we learn that the image modality (at least with resnet50) is not contributing, redirecting effort toward RNA encoder or profile-setting improvements. Under a tight budget, resolving the modality question first prevents wasting experiments on hyperparameter tuning of a potentially unhelpful modality.

Evidence: config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) achieved 0.527 acc / 0.510 F1, a clear ~4% improvement over the rna_only baseline (config_001, 0.485 acc). This confirms that adding a ResNet50 image branch with concat fusion is beneficial. However, all experiments so far use singleprofile; the multiprofile axis is entirely untested and represents the largest remaining source of uncertainty about whether additional per-cell profile information can further boost performance. Question tested: Does switching from singleprofile to multiprofile (with avgpool aggregation) improve on the validated multimodal+concat setup, while keeping RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (resnet50), and fusion (concat) identical to config_016? This isolates the profile-setting effect. Why this is the best next experiment: It is the minimal, cleanest extension of our best-performing configuration along the most impactful untested design axis. A positive result would justify investing further in multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation, other encoders); a null or negative result would let us redirect budget toward RNA/image encoder choices and fusion strategy, avoiding wasted experiments on a less productive axis. Under a tight budget, resolving this binary question about multiprofile value is more informative than, e.g., testing weighted vs. concat fusion on singleprofile, where the expected delta is smaller.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the clear best at 0.619 acc, showing that multiprofile aggregation is the dominant design lever (+0.092 over singleprofile multimodal). However, we have no evidence on whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for combining multiple profiles. This experiment (config_020) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other settings identical to config_018, cleanly isolating the effect of the aggregation strategy. Under a limited budget, this is the highest-information single-variable test: if transformer substantially improves over avgpool, it reshapes the search toward transformer-based aggregation for all future encoder/fusion combinations; if it is comparable, we can deprioritize transformer and focus remaining budget on RNA/image encoder upgrades or fusion strategy.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the clear best at acc=0.619/F1=0.610, and we've confirmed that multiprofile+avgpool is strongly preferred over singleprofile and transformer aggregation. However, the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted) has only been tested in the singleprofile setting (config_016, concat) and has never been compared in the multiprofile+avgpool regime where performance is highest. Question: Does weighted fusion outperform concat fusion when combined with the proven multiprofile+avgpool pipeline? This is a single-variable A/B test against our best result, isolating the fusion mechanism. Why best next experiment: It is the lowest-risk, highest-information extension of the strongest evidence—either it confirms concat is sufficient (freeing us to explore image/RNA encoder upgrades) or it reveals that fusion weighting is a meaningful lever (opening a clear exploitation path). Under a tight budget, resolving this one binary design question before committing to larger architectural changes (ViT-L, scGPT, scVI) is the most efficient use of the next run.

Evidence: The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.639). Key findings: (1) multimodal >> RNA-only, (2) multiprofile >> singleprofile (~9% gain), (3) avgpool > transformer for aggregation, (4) weighted > concat for fusion. The one major design axis untested within the winning configuration is the image encoder: we have only used ResNet50, while ImageNet ViT-L is available and substantially more expressive. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder from ResNet50 to ViT-L further improve the already-strong multimodal pipeline, or is the image contribution already saturated? Why this experiment: config_025 is the minimal, direct extension of the current best (only swapping the image encoder), so any performance change is cleanly attributable to encoder capacity. Given that the image modality contributes meaningfully (multimodal vs. RNA-only gap), resolving whether a stronger visual backbone helps is the highest-information next step under a limited budget, and it avoids confounding multiple changes.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.639 acc. We have strong evidence that multiprofile + avgpool + weighted fusion is the optimal architecture, and that resnet50 ≈ imagenet_vit_l. However, the RNA encoder has only been tested as pca_n2000 across all multimodal experiments. Question: config_031 is a clean single-variable swap of the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while holding the best-known architecture (multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) constant. This directly tests whether a learned, biologically-informed RNA representation (scVI) can outperform a linear PCA projection in the multimodal setting. Why this is the best next experiment: The RNA encoder is a fundamental, high-impact design choice that remains completely unexplored in multimodal settings. A positive result would open a productive new search direction (scvi/scgpt encoders); a null result would confirm PCA sufficiency and let us focus remaining budget on other axes. This is more informative than testing transformer+weighted (where avgpool's ~4% advantage over transformer with concat makes a reversal unlikely) or re-testing image encoder variants (already shown to be near-equivalent).

Evidence: The current best (config_031, scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc 0.678) clearly outperforms the prior best (config_019, pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc 0.639), confirming that the learned scvi encoder is a major driver. With pca_n2000, resnet50 and imagenet_vit_l were nearly equivalent (0.639 vs 0.635), but that comparison was made with a linear PCA representation. Question: Does the richer, learned scvi_n200 representation interact synergistically with the larger ViT image encoder, or does resnet50 remain sufficient? This is a single-variable swap from the current best (only image encoder changes), making it a clean, high-information experiment. Why best next: It directly exploits the strongest validated direction (scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool + weighted) while resolving the one remaining uncertainty in the best configuration's design, giving the highest expected information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

The current best (config_037: scvi_n200 + vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706) has established that multimodal/multiprofile/avgpool/weighted is the optimal architecture, and that scvi_n200 substantially outperforms pca_n2000. However, the scgpt RNA encoder is completely untested in any multimodal setting, representing the largest remaining source of uncertainty in the design space. config_049 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) is a clean, single-variable comparison against config_037—only the RNA encoder changes. If scgpt surpasses scvi_n200, we identify a new best configuration; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 as the superior encoder and can confidently stop exploring that dimension. Under a limited budget, this experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most impactful untested design choice while staying anchored to the proven-optimal settings in all other dimensions.

The current best configuration (config_037: scvi_n200 + ViT-L + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706) has established that scvi_n200 and ViT-L are the strongest encoders, and avgpool > transformer was observed only under the weaker pca encoder (config_018 vs 020: 0.619 vs 0.579). The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation could outperform avgpool when paired with scvi's richer, learned nonlinear representations—scvi encodes cell-level latent structure that may benefit from attention-based cross-profile interaction in a way pca's linear projections do not. Config_039 is a single-variable change from the best config (avgpool→transformer), making the comparison clean and directly informative. If transformer matches or beats avgpool here, it opens a new optimization axis; if it confirms avgpool superiority, it consolidates the design and lets us focus remaining budget on other dimensions. This is the highest-information experiment because it resolves the one untested design choice in the best-performing setting.
